name: @pull-fm/bff
//scripts.refresh:mb-canonical: Named and shaped exactly like the four jobs above so infra/scripts/check-job-schedule.mjs can assert it the same way: a pnpm command here, a compiled entrypoint in src/scripts/, and a systemd unit that invokes it. Without this line the entrypoint existed and NOTHING COULD NAME IT, which is the gap that checker was written to catch.

IT CANNOT RUN INSIDE THE BFF IMAGE, and that is not a defect in this line - it is the reason the shipped timer does not use it. The entrypoint spawns infra/mb-loader/mb-canonical-load.sh, which needs psql, zstd, tar, curl and awk; the runtime image is node:22-alpine plus dumb-init and carries none of them, and the loader script is not in the image either (the build ships `pnpm deploy --prod /out`, JavaScript only). So `pullfm-job refresh-mb-canonical` would fail on a missing binary, not on anything this repository could fix from here. infra/mb-loader/systemd/ runs the loader on the HOST instead, the same way infra/backup does, and infra/mb-loader/systemd/README.md explains the choice.

This command stays because it is the right entrypoint from a checkout, from CI, and from any image that does have the four binaries - and because MbCanonicalRefresh is what holds the cross-node advisory lock and turns the loader's exit code into the 0/1/2 contract.
